verdict: Reddit's revenue jumped 69% to $663M as ad sales surged — and with costs growing far more slowly, net income jumped eightfold to $204M, a 31% margin.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — powered by more users, more time on site, and better ad targeting.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly data licensing — deals that let AI companies train on Reddit's public posts — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the product and the ad platform — up 8% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning advertisers and users — up 67% YoY, the fastest-growing cost line.

takeaways.title: Growth accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue growth picked up to 69%, powered by advertising (+74%) as daily users hit 126.8M — Reddit is still getting bigger and better at selling ads against its communities.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped eightfold
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $26M a year ago to $204M. Total costs grew just 24% while revenue grew 69%, so most of the new revenue dropped straight to the bottom line.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $311M — 47% of revenue — and Reddit ended the quarter holding $2.8B of cash and marketable securities.

otherDetail: Other income of $23M, net — mostly interest earned on Reddit's $2.8B pile of cash and marketable securities.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to the nearest $M, following the same convention as Reddit's other pages; the statements report in thousands (advertising $624.7M, other revenue $38.7M).
